Clipora and ClipboardFusion: choose your workflow.

ClipboardFusion combines clipboard management with text cleanup, macros and triggers. Clipora also covers reusable history and automation, with a different native workspace and sync setup.

Reviewed 29 October 2026 · Clipora editorial

What is included and what differs

Documentation comparison, checked 29 October 2026. Clipora baseline: Store package 2.0.5.0 x64. These are documented workflows, not head-to-head speed, reliability or security benchmarks. “Not verified” does not mean unavailable.

Pick by automation and sync needs

ClipboardFusion may be a good fit if its scrubbing, macro ecosystem or hosted account-sync workflow meets your needs. Do not assume that pins, images, macros or triggers require its Pro edition; its official feature table includes those locally in Free.

Clipora is an option for a native Windows workspace with compact quick access, a persistent organized library, offline Windows OCR and portable encrypted backups. Its optional private-server/folder sync takes a different setup from a managed cloud account.

Check the edition and current terms

This page uses ClipboardFusion 6.3 as its stable release baseline. The separately available 6.4 beta is not silently treated as stable. Prices, license terms and companion availability can change, so use the official pages before making a purchase or choosing it for business use.

The companion page lists additional platforms, but this review has not installed those companions or verified current feature parity. Clipora does not currently offer native iOS, Android or macOS clients.

A comparison of documented behavior

No ClipboardFusion trial, cloud-sync account or payment was used for this article. We do not claim measured performance, comparative security or guaranteed compatibility with every application. Both products should be evaluated with harmless data in the applications you actually use.

Clipboard contents can be sensitive. Read the selected product’s storage, sync and macro policies before enabling automation.
